title: Define model-family taxonomy + mapping rules for kernel selector v2 (incl unknown/experimental handling)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Problem
Selector v2 is table-driven and needs stable keys for “model family” to select kernels safely across architectures and flags (e.g., GQA/MQA, sliding window, MoE). Today we have a mix of ad-hoc heuristics and per-model exceptions. We need a well-defined taxonomy + deterministic mapping rules that (a) work with partial metadata, (b) fail safely for unknown families, and (c) are stable enough for registry versioning.

Goals
- Define canonical set of model-family identifiers used by kernel registry entries (human readable + stable).
- Define deterministic mapping rules from model metadata -> (family, variant flags) with explicit precedence.
- Define behavior for unknown/experimental architectures: safe kernel set + telemetry + optional fallback to v1.
- Provide test fixtures + conformance expectations so adding a new family doesn’t regress existing mappings.

Non-goals
- Writing kernels.
- Full model catalog metadata standardization across the company (this ticket is runtime-facing mapping for selector v2).

Proposed taxonomy (v0)
We split taxonomy into:
(A) Family: high-level architecture lineage used in registry row matching.
(B) Variant flags: used to select sub-row/override within a family (e.g., GQA vs MHA, sliding window enabled).

Family identifiers (initial)
- llama (Llama 2/3 + close derivatives that keep attention semantics; many open models fall here)
- mistral (Mistral 7B, etc.)
- qwen (Qwen 2.x)
- gemma (Gemma 2.x)
- mixtral (MoE; treated separately due to routing/expert patterns)
- unknown (explicit bucket; never gets a “fast-but-risky” kernel)

Variant flags (initial; keep small)
- attn_kind: mha | gqa | mqa
  - derived from num_key_value_heads vs num_attention_heads
- sliding_window: true | false
  - derived from sliding_window or equivalent config key
- rope_scaling: none | linear | dynamic | yarn | other
  - used only for “safe/unsafe” gating initially; not for fine-grained kernel choice unless needed
- moe: true | false
  - derived from config (num_experts / architectures) (primarily for mixtral)

Mapping inputs
Primary sources (in order):
1) Explicit runtime override (config): model_family_override / variant overrides (used for emergency ops).
2) Model metadata embedded in model artifact (HF-like config JSON): model_type, architectures, num_attention_heads, num_key_value_heads, sliding_window, rope_scaling, etc.
3) Redwood model catalog metadata (if present): model_family_hint (string), validated flags.
4) Heuristic fallback from known model name patterns (only as last resort; must be guarded + logged).

Deterministic mapping algorithm (v0)
1) If model_family_override is set -> return that family + any explicit variant overrides; emit telemetry selector_mapping_source=override.
2) Else if model catalog provides model_family_hint and it’s in allowed set -> return it; source=catalog.
3) Else parse config:
   a) Determine candidate family:
      - if model_type or architectures indicate Qwen -> family=qwen
      - if indicate Mistral -> family=mistral
      - if indicate Gemma -> family=gemma
      - if indicate Mixtral/MoE -> family=mixtral
      - else if indicates Llama-like -> family=llama
      - else family=unknown
   b) Compute variant flags:
      - attn_kind:
        - if num_key_value_heads missing -> attn_kind=unknown (treat as mha in safe-kernel selection)
        - else if num_key_value_heads == num_attention_heads -> mha
        - else if num_key_value_heads == 1 -> mqa
        - else gqa
      - sliding_window: true if config contains non-null sliding_window and it’s > 0, else false
      - rope_scaling: normalize known values; unknown -> other
      - moe: true if config suggests experts / mixture-of-experts, else false
   c) If family=unknown -> attach reason codes (missing model_type, unrecognized architectures, etc.) for logs.
4) If the computed family conflicts with moe flag (e.g., family=llama but moe=true) -> prefer family=mixtral IF architectures strongly indicate MoE; otherwise keep family and mark mapping_conflict=true.
5) Return (family, flags) and mapping_source=config/heuristic.

Unknown/experimental behavior (safety requirements)
- family=unknown must never select an experimental kernel. It must choose from “safe kernel set” (per GPU) OR fall back to selector v1 depending on config.
- Default behavior for hosted: selector v2 can still run, but kernel choice must be from safe set; if safe set missing on that GPU -> fallback to v1.
- Default behavior for dedicated/private: allow customer/operator to opt into v2 unknown-family safe set vs forced v1 (config knob).
- Always emit telemetry when family=unknown:
  - selector_family=unknown
  - unknown_reason_bucket (bounded cardinality)
  - model_config_fingerprint (hashed) for grouping without PII

Registry matching contract
- Registry rows are keyed by (family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_normalized) with optional constraints on variant flags.
- Matching precedence:
  1) exact match on family + variant constraints
  2) family match with fewer constraints (more general)
  3) safe set for gpu_sku
  4) fallback to selector v1
- Tie-break must be deterministic: prefer most-specific row (highest “specificity score”); if still tied, prefer highest registry version then lexical kernel_id.

Deliverables
- Documented taxonomy + mapping rules (this ticket) and code implementation in model-family detection module.
- Unit tests with fixtures for:
  - llama (mha, gqa)
  - mistral
  - qwen
  - mixtral/moe
  - missing metadata -> unknown
  - conflicting metadata -> conflict path
- Runtime logs/telemetry fields for mapping_source, family, flags, conflict, unknown_reason_bucket.
- Clear instructions for adding a new family (what metadata is required, where to add tests, how to update registry).

Acceptance criteria
- Given a model config fixture set, mapping output is stable and deterministic.
- Unknown-family models do not crash selection; they pick safe kernels or v1 fallback.
- Cardinality-safe telemetry (no raw model names in labels).
- Reviewed by kernel selection lead + SRE/telemetry stakeholder.

comments: 2026-01-08 — Grace Kim: +1 on splitting family vs flags. Please keep flags minimal for v1 of registry; we can expand later once we see perf deltas by flag. Also request: mapping must be stable even if HF config has extra fields we don’t understand.

2026-01-09 — Yuki Sato: For GPU-specific safe kernels, can we ensure unknown-family always routes to kernels that are known to work on A10 (we’ve seen odd shape asserts on older SMs)? Suggest safe set per gpu_sku_normalized, not global.

2026-01-11 — Thomas Baird: Telemetry labels: do NOT emit raw architectures[] or model names. Suggest unknown_reason_bucket with a small enum and a hashed config fingerprint (trace-only is fine; metrics must be bucketed).

2026-01-13 — Omar El-Sayed: Scheduler can pass prefill/decode and seq bucket; mapping code should be independent of request context (pure function of model metadata + overrides), otherwise we’ll get hard-to-debug drift.
2026-01-16 — Noah Patel: Implemented mapping_source precedence and conflict marking. Added fixtures for llama/mistral/qwen/mixtral plus missing-metadata -> unknown. PR up: pr_18441.

2026-01-19 — Allison Grant (SRE/obs standards): Please ensure unknown_reason_bucket is bounded and documented. Also ensure mapping_conflict increments a counter—we’ve been bitten by silent “best effort” mapping hiding real metadata issues.
2026-02-03 — Grace Kim: Marking done after merge + docs update. Follow-up: add a short ‘How to add a new family’ section to the kernel registry taxonomy page when we onboard next architecture.

2026-02-10 — Talia Benson: Closing ticket. Note: unknown-family fallback bug surfaced during canary and was fixed in pr_18526; mapping rules doc now explicitly calls out safe set / v1 fallback behavior.
